reuse_note: Facts marked reused: true are copied from articles/2026-11-13-marriage-licence-requirements/02-research-A.json (original IDs in use_note), checked 2026-11-13. Legal confirmations name the authority (celebrant, BDM registry, AGD), not the Wedded Advisor.

facts.claim: Section 44 of the Marriage Act 1961: a marriage shall not be solemnised unless at least 2 persons who are, or appear to the person solemnising the marriage to be, over the age of 18 years are present as witnesses.
facts.publisher: Federal Register of Legislation, Marriage Act 1961 (compilation 9 July 2024)
facts.use_note: Reused from requirements A F-012. Note 'appear to the celebrant to be' over 18: the celebrant judges age; the Act sets no ID rule for witnesses in this section.

facts.claim: On the wedding day, 3 marriage certificates must be signed by the couple, the authorised celebrant, and 2 witnesses over 18. The celebrant gives the couple a certificate of marriage on the day, which is a ceremonial certificate. Within 14 days the celebrant submits the paperwork to the BDM registry of the state or territory where the marriage took place.
facts.use_note: Reused from requirements A F-016. Core 'what witnesses sign' fact.

facts.claim: Since 12 June 2024 the celebrant must be physically present to solemnise a marriage, together with the parties and 2 witnesses.
facts.use_note: Reused from requirements A F-006. Ceremony witnesses cannot attend by video link.

facts.claim: Authorised witnesses for signing the NOIM. In Australia: an authorised celebrant, a justice of the peace, a barrister or solicitor, a medical practitioner, or a member of the Australian Federal Police or a state or territory police force. Outside Australia: an Australian Consular Officer, an Australian Diplomatic Officer, a notary public, or a Commonwealth or Austrade employee authorised under the Consular Fees Act 1955.
facts.publisher: Attorney-General's Department, Notice of Intended Marriage form
facts.use_note: Reused from requirements A F-004. This is a different role from the 2 ceremony witnesses: a NOIM witness is a listed official; ceremony witnesses are any 2 people over 18.

facts.claim: Since 12 June 2024 the NOIM may be witnessed in person or remotely by audio-visual link. If the couple is in Australia, the remote witness (which can be a celebrant) must also be in Australia; if the couple is outside Australia, the authorised witness (who cannot be a celebrant) must also be outside Australia. You cannot witness online a NOIM for a person or couple outside Australia.
facts.publisher: Attorney-General's Department, Notice of Intended Marriage
facts.use_note: Reused from requirements A F-005. Video-link scope: NOIM witnessing only, never the ceremony (F-003).
